chunks: My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Ḥusain ibn ‘Uthmān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), and Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from someone whose name he mentioned, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him).

He said: I do not foresee any (newborn baby) whose mouth is opened with water from the Euphrates River to be anything other than from among our Shia. Ibn Abī ‘Umayr said: And I do not know him except as Ibn Sīnān, except that he had narrated it to me. And Ibn Abī ‘Umayr narrated from some of our companions who said: Two spouts flow from Paradise into the Euphrates.

key_terms.شِيعَةً: Shia, followers or partisans (of the Ahl al-Bayt).
key_terms.يُحَنَّكُ: To moisten the mouth of a newborn with something sweet or soft, a traditional practice.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of drinking from the Euphrates River in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition linking the Euphrates' spiritual purity to the identity of the Shia, a concept rooted in the river's association with the Ahl al-Bayt's lineage and divine favor. The narration highlights two spouts (mizaban) flowing from Paradise into the river, symbolizing a tangible connection between the celestial realm and the faithful who consume its water. This elevates the Euphrates from a geographical feature to a sacred sign (ayah) of Shi'a allegiance and eschatological hope.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 11. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Ḥusain ibn ‘Uthmān, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: I do not foresee any (newborn baby) whose mouth is opened with water from the Euphrates River to be anything other than from among our Shia. The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from someone whose name he mentioned, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (a.s.).
